rationale: Both responses centre stall detection on a per-request emission heartbeat or rate rather than total duration, add GPU-side corroboration, use multi-window burn rates for SLOs and split pages from tickets. B has valuable additions: explicit phase gating so prefill, eviction pauses and cache rebuilds are not flagged, a session-cache deadlock signature, KV growth as a progress cue, and alerting before the watchdog fires. However, B's canonical stall alert requires SM occupancy below 5%, which misses a busy-but-unproductive stall such as a stuck verification loop or graph replay error. Its burn-rate windows are also unconventionally specified. A's diagnostic table is more insightful. It separates a frozen heartbeat with an idle GPU (hang), a busy GPU (stuck loop) and memory backpressure at the cap (capacity, ticket not page). It correctly treats near-zero acceptance as degraded-but-progressing, tracked as a distribution shift. A also gives sound granularity rules (no per-token metrics, traces at full sampling when the heartbeat fires) and scheduler-level memory accounting. On balance A's discrimination logic is sharper.
